mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is active whenever the rate is at historically low levels, regardless of trend.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings contraction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (indicating monetary easing) and rise in the unemployment rate (indicating labor market deterioration) signals an impending recession, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decline > 0.25pp over 3 months AND UNRATE rise > 0.2pp over 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both FEDFUNDS declines > 0.25pp over 3 months and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing boom regime (HOUST > 1400 thousand units), strong consumer demand for housing stimulates economic activity and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1400.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 265 (indicating elevated inflation) typically triggers expectations of monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 265.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high housing starts (HOUST > 1400 thousand units) and low industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals a demand-supply imbalance where strong consumer demand is not met by production capacity, leading to inflationary pressures and potential monetary tightening, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1400 and INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (INDPRO < 100), reduced industrial output leads to higher input costs and lower corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.
